attacks.claim: The QA table reports Pass and 0 misdelivered texts for a staff pilot that the rollout schedules for Nov 2-6. Today is 2026-10-26, so those results cannot yet exist. The launch decision relies on them.
attacks.evidence: "Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds) | 0 misdelivered texts; 2 copy fixes shipped and re-verified" / "Nov 2-6: flags on for staff cards only (pilot above)."

attacks.claim: The fixed public announcement says alerts are for every cardholder, but juvenile cards cannot see or use the SMS option. The 10:00 public statement is inaccurate for that group.
attacks.evidence: "Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder." vs "juvenile cards do not show it"

attacks.claim: Phone number and consent record (timestamp, IP, checkbox version) have no stated retention or deletion trigger on STOP or account closure. Deletion is tied only to permanent SMS withdrawal.
attacks.evidence: "Phone number and consent record (timestamp, IP, checkbox text version) are stored in the patron record" / ABSENT: retention on STOP or account closure

attacks.claim: The $900 hard cap stops SMS only. Cap-triggered fallback to automated phone calls for every opted-in patron has no cost or volume estimate, so total notification spend is not bounded.
attacks.evidence: "On cap, texts stop and every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call, which stays on file)" / ABSENT: phone-call cost or volume

attacks.claim: Patrons who chose SMS instead of email may have no working previous channel on cap or rollback. The artifact does not confirm that the phone-call fallback reaches them, so the 'no alert is lost' claim is not demonstrated for them.
attacks.evidence: "in addition to (or instead of) the current email" / "so no alert is lost"

attacks.claim: The locker rollback remaps pickup_location but does not say whether already-sent single-use codes are invalidated. A code sent by text could still open a cell after its hold moves to the desk.
attacks.evidence: "holds currently assigned to a locker ... are remapped to the branch desk by scripts/remap_locker_holds.sql" / ABSENT: code invalidation step

attacks.claim: All cardholders get flags on at once at 09:00 with no percentage ramp after the staff pilot. The 10:00 announcement then makes any later rollback visible to patrons who already know the feature and may hold codes.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 9 09:00: flags on for all cardholders; announcement goes out at 10:00"

attacks.claim: The locker kiosk carries the higher-stakes access flow and ADA features, but QA covers only the opt-in web form with NVDA and VoiceOver. Kiosk screen-reader, TalkBack, and high-contrast checks are absent.
attacks.evidence: "Opt-in form with NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver iOS; 320/768/1280 px layouts | Pass" / "screen has high-contrast mode, audio guidance through a headphone jack"

attacks.claim: The only legal review cited covers the privacy policy. The artifact records no review of the SMS consent text or the TCPA/CTIA frequency disclosure.
attacks.evidence: "Privacy policy section 4 updated to list SMS; legal review complete (ticket LGL-118)." / ABSENT: legal review of consent text

attacks.claim: The provider retains message bodies for 30 days, and those bodies contain locker codes linked to a phone number. The artifact does not confirm that the 2025-03 DPA covers hold-ready and locker-code content, and asserts the notification log is consistent with the no-borrowing-history policy without showing it.
attacks.evidence: "it retains message logs 30 days and is barred from marketing use" / "consistent with our no-borrowing-history policy"

attacks.claim: The sample text gives one code for two holds, but codes are described as single-use. The artifact does not say whether one code opens both items or whether a second code is needed, so one hold could become uncollectable after the first pickup.
attacks.evidence: "2 holds ready at Oak St locker. Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14." / "Codes are single-use"

attacks.claim: QA ran against the provider in test mode, a staff-room locker, and a $5 test cap. This is disclosed. It verifies the fallback logic but not production behaviour at the $900 cap or with live carriers.
attacks.evidence: "against the production SMS provider account in test mode and a locker bank in the staff room." / "Spend cap reached (test cap $5)"

attacks.claim: The 70% ($630) ops alert is part of the spend-control design but has no QA row, so ops receipt is unverified.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: QA row for 70% alert. "alert to ops at 70%"

attacks.claim: The staff pilot's number of real sends is not stated. Staff cards are not representative of juvenile, Spanish-preferring, or carrier-mix patrons.
attacks.evidence: "Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds)"

attacks.claim: Locker codes travel as plaintext SMS and may show on the lock screen. Residual risk is bounded by the required card scan or card number plus PIN, but the artifact does not state this as an accepted risk.
attacks.evidence: "Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14." / "The locker opens only after the patron scans their library card (or enters card number + PIN ...) AND enters the code."

attacks.claim: The 5-attempt lockout is per cell. The artifact states no per-patron or cross-cell attempt limit, and a third party can trigger lockouts to deny a legitimate pickup.
attacks.evidence: "5 wrong attempts lock the cell and alert branch staff" / ABSENT: per-patron or cross-cell limit

attacks.claim: A locker bank outage after hours leaves codes uncollectable until the 4-hour vendor SLA is met. The only stated alternative is the service desk during opening hours.
attacks.evidence: "vendor SLA 4 h on-site" / "Holds stay collectible at the service desk during opening hours"

attacks.claim: The pickup deadline is a fixed date. The artifact does not say whether it runs from ready time or send time, and quiet-hours queueing can leave less pickup time than the text implies. Weekend and 24/7 locker alignment is not stated.
attacks.evidence: "pick up by Sat Nov 14." / "anything later is queued to 08:00" / ABSENT: deadline anchor

attacks.claim: The 38,000 texts/month forecast has no stated opt-in rate, holds-per-month basis, or peak-day volume, so headroom under the $900 cap cannot be checked. No load test is cited for the 09:00 enablement or the 08:00 queue flush.
attacks.evidence: "Forecast 38,000 texts/month at about $0.012 all-in" / ABSENT: opt-in rate, load test

attacks.claim: SMS delivery and locker pickup each depend on a single vendor. The artifact states no exit path, data-export plan, or hosting region for the messaging provider.
attacks.evidence: "the SMS provider is an existing vendor under a signed DPA" / ABSENT: exit plan or residency

attacks.claim: Guardian opt-in sends juvenile hold-ready notices to the guardian's phone. The artifact does not analyse this against the privacy section.
attacks.evidence: "guardians can opt in with their own number on the linked guardian account" / ABSENT: privacy analysis

attacks.claim: The locker remap was tested on 1,200 staging rows. Production row count, runtime, and staff hours for the shelf moves are not stated.
attacks.evidence: "scripts/remap_locker_holds.sql (tested in staging on 1,200 rows)"

attacks.claim: Flags are copied verbatim from staging with no automated parity check, so environment drift depends on manual smoke testing.
attacks.evidence: "config/prod.flags.yaml copied verbatim" / ABSENT: automated flag-parity check

attacks.claim: No alert or dashboard metric covers fallback activation or cap-reached state, so degradation to the fallback channel could go unnoticed.
attacks.evidence: "Dashboard: texts sent, delivery rate, STOP rate, queue depth, locker cell status." / ABSENT: fallback-activated alert
